$comment: Rule catalog — data safety. Standard 49. Destructive-by-default routes to ai.destructive-approval (Standard 2 R3) rather than being duplicated here.

rules.title: Destructive migrations have a recovery path and are verified
rules.description: No destructive migration runs without a rollback or recovery strategy where recovery is feasible, and no migration is assumed to have succeeded without verification.
rules.rationale: Two halves of one discipline: knowing how to get back, and knowing whether you need to. A migration that reported success without checking is indistinguishable, when it matters, from one that failed silently.
rules.remediation: Write the rollback or the snapshot procedure before running, and verify the post-migration state rather than inferring it from an exit code.
rules.$assuranceNote: Whether a rollback strategy exists is a claim about an operational plan, not about a file in the repository.

rules.title: User data is not silently discarded
rules.description: No user data is dropped without the user being told: no truncated field, no swallowed batch item, no record that failed validation while the caller was told the write succeeded.
rules.rationale: Silently is the qualifier and it is internal to the prohibition, so no exception can be legitimate. Rejecting data at the boundary with a structured error is correct behaviour and is not this rule's subject.
rules.remediation: Report the rejected items in the result, using the partial-success shape Standard 14 R5 provides.
rules.$assuranceNote: Requires knowing which data was the user's, which no scan of a repository establishes.

rules.title: Historical and audit data are not rewritten to fit a new schema
rules.description: No audit or historical record is backfilled with values it never carried in order to satisfy a new schema. Versioning the schema, adding nullable columns, and migrating into a new store while retaining the original are the supported approaches.
rules.rationale: An audit record's entire value is that it says what was true at the time. Backfilling replaces a fact with a guess, which is why no exception exists.
rules.remediation: Version the record schema and read old records under their own version, or migrate into a new store and retain the original.
rules.$assuranceNote: Requires knowing which store holds the audit record, which is a project fact rather than a code property.

rules.title: Production data is not used unsafely outside production
rules.description: No production dataset is used in a development or test environment without masking, subsetting, and access control. An exception for a defect that only reproduces against real data expires with the investigation.
rules.rationale: Unsafely is the qualifier: a masked and access-controlled copy is legitimate practice. A full dump on a developer machine is one of the most common routes by which a controlled dataset leaves its controls.
rules.remediation: Mask and subset the copy, hold it in an access-controlled environment, and delete it when the work is done.
rules.$assuranceNote: Whether a dataset came from production is not visible in a repository at all.
